1	// Package bench is the forgemark benchmark engine: it drives real git
2	// push/clone operations against one target forge and reports per-level
3	// results. Frontends (the CLI, and any interactive UI) are thin layers over
4	// Runner; they observe a run live through the exported Sink.
5	package bench
6	
7	import (
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"net/url"
11		"strconv"
12		"strings"
13		"time"
14	
15		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
16	)
17	
18	// Target is one forge to benchmark: where to connect and how to authenticate.
19	// Supplying TokenURL or Jurisdiction selects the entiredb path (node
20	// discovery, account access token presented directly); they mean nothing to
21	// any other forge, so their presence is the signal — no separate target-kind
22	// field.
23	type Target struct {
24		Name      string   // display label; empty defaults to the remote base URL
25		Remote    string   // base URL of the forge, e.g. https://gitlab.com
26		Repos     []string // repo paths appended to Remote verbatim
27		User      string   // basic-auth username (default x-access-token; token forges ignore it)
28		Secret    string   `json:"-"` // credential secret (forge token, or the entiredb account access token); json:"-" so no marshal path can ever leak it
29		Insecure  bool     // skip TLS verification
30		ObjectFmt string   // "auto" | "sha1" | "sha256"
31	
32		// entiredb. Presence selects the path; none of the three is dialed.
33		TokenURL     string
34		Jurisdiction string
35		ClientID     string
36	}
37	
38	// Hard safety caps, not tuning suggestions: a single host can't generate a
39	// meaningful benchmark anywhere near them, and unbounded values from the
40	// server API would otherwise reach make([]*agent, c), c goroutine spawns,
41	// and per-sample retention for the whole window — panic/OOM territory.
42	//
43	// Known ceiling, deliberately NOT capped: within these limits, retained-sample
44	// memory still scales with measured throughput (a 6h max-concurrency level
45	// against a very fast target reaches 10⁸+ Samples). That is the cost of the
46	// exact percentiles LevelResult promises for real runs — the bounded
47	// alternative is approximation, which is exactly the trade the demo target
48	// makes and real results must not. An aggregate agent-hours cap would reject
49	// valid configs to protect operators from their own machine's RAM; the ops
50	// have to actually happen for the memory to exist, so the operator is load
51	// generator and victim at once. If this ever bites in practice, the fix is
52	// compact retention (durations only, errors grouped online), not a cap here.
53	const (
54		maxConcurrency = 4096          // agents per level
55		maxLevels      = 16            // levels per sweep
56		maxDuration    = 6 * time.Hour // measured window per level
57		maxWarmup      = time.Hour     // warm-up per level
58	
59		// Commit content is the same class of API-reachable allocation: FileSize
60		// goes straight into make([]byte, FileSize) in every agent (a near-MaxInt
61		// value is a runtime panic that kills the whole process, not just the
62		// run), and FilesMax × FileSize is the working set every agent keeps in
63		// its in-memory worktree.
64		maxFilesMax    = 1024     // files per commit
65		maxFileSize    = 16 << 20 // bytes per file
66		maxCommitBytes = 64 << 20 // files-max × file-size, one commit's payload
67	)
68	
69	// Workload is the target-independent shape of a run: strategy, sweep, and
70	// commit content. One Workload is shared by every target of a comparison run.
71	type Workload struct {
72		RunID        string
73		Strategy     string // branch | repo | clone | session
74		RefNamespace string // ref namespace pushes land under; "" = DefaultRefNamespace
75		BranchPrefix string // prepended verbatim inside the namespace, before the run ID
76		Concurrency  []int
77		Duration     time.Duration
78		Warmup       time.Duration
79		Commit       CommitConfig
80	
81		// session/clone strategies
82		SessionCommits int
83		CloneDepth     int
84		BaseRef        string
85	}
86	
87	// Validate applies the target-independent checks that parseFlags used to do,
88	// so the server rejects a bad workload with the same errors the CLI reports.
89	func (w Workload) Validate() error {
90		switch w.Strategy {
91		case "branch", "repo", "clone", "session":
92		default:
93			return fmt.Errorf("invalid -strategy %q (branch|repo|clone|session)", w.Strategy)
94		}
95		if w.Strategy == "session" && w.SessionCommits < 1 {
96			return errors.New("-session-commits must be >= 1")
97		}
98		if w.CloneDepth < 0 {
99			return errors.New("-clone-depth must be >= 0 (0 = full history)")
100		}
101		if len(w.Concurrency) == 0 {
102			return errors.New("no concurrency levels")
103		}
104		if len(w.Concurrency) > maxLevels {
105			return fmt.Errorf("too many concurrency levels: %d (max %d)", len(w.Concurrency), maxLevels)
106		}
107		for _, n := range w.Concurrency {
108			if n < 1 || n > maxConcurrency {
109				return fmt.Errorf("invalid concurrency %d (must be 1..%d)", n, maxConcurrency)
110			}
111		}
112		if w.Duration <= 0 || w.Duration > maxDuration {
113			return fmt.Errorf("-duration must be > 0 and <= %s", maxDuration)
114		}
115		if w.Warmup < 0 || w.Warmup > maxWarmup {
116			return fmt.Errorf("-warmup must be >= 0 and <= %s", maxWarmup)
117		}
118		if w.Strategy != "clone" {
119			if w.Commit.FilesMin < 1 {
120				return errors.New("-files-min must be >= 1 (a commit needs a change to push)")
121			}
122			if w.Commit.FilesMax < w.Commit.FilesMin {
123				return errors.New("-files-max < -files-min")
124			}
125			if w.Commit.FilesMax > maxFilesMax {
126				return fmt.Errorf("-files-max must be <= %d", maxFilesMax)
127			}
128			if w.Commit.FileSize < 1 {
129				return errors.New("-file-size must be >= 1 (empty blobs reproduce → ErrEmptyCommit)")
130			}
131			if w.Commit.FileSize > maxFileSize {
132				return fmt.Errorf("-file-size must be <= %d (%dMiB)", maxFileSize, maxFileSize>>20)
133			}
134			// Both factors already fit comfortably in int64, so the product can't
135			// overflow this aggregate check.
136			if int64(w.Commit.FilesMax)*int64(w.Commit.FileSize) > maxCommitBytes {
137				return fmt.Errorf("-files-max × -file-size must be <= %dMiB per commit", maxCommitBytes>>20)
138			}
139		}
140		// Validate the assembled ref, not the parts alone: validity is context-dependent
141		// (a trailing "/" or bare word is fine mid-ref, invalid standalone). c/a are arbitrary —
142		// only the namespace and prefix can invalidate it — so these parse-time checks cover
143		// the whole sweep. The namespace is checked first, on its own, so a bad namespace
144		// isn't reported as a bad prefix.
145		runID := w.RunID
146		if runID == "" {
147			runID = "fmX"
148		}
149		ns := w.Namespace()
150		if !strings.HasPrefix(ns, "refs/") || ns == "refs/" {
151			return fmt.Errorf("invalid -ref-namespace %q: must be refs/<name>/", w.RefNamespace)
152		}
153		if err := plumbing.ReferenceName(DestRef(ns, "", runID, 1, 0)).Validate(); err != nil {
154			return fmt.Errorf("invalid -ref-namespace %q: %w", w.RefNamespace, err)
155		}
156		if err := plumbing.ReferenceName(DestRef(ns, w.BranchPrefix, runID, 1, 0)).Validate(); err != nil {
157			return fmt.Errorf("invalid -branch-prefix %q: %w", w.BranchPrefix, err)
158		}
159		return nil
160	}
161	
162	// DefaultRefNamespace is where bench refs land unless -ref-namespace says
163	// otherwise. It is deliberately NOT refs/heads/: receive-pack does the same
164	// work for any ref (pack unpack, connectivity check, ref CAS), but a branch
165	// additionally triggers whatever the forge runs post-receive — search
166	// ingestion, CI, webhooks, branch UI — which costs money and rate-limit
167	// budget on the target and is invisible to the push latency this tool
168	// measures anyway. A private namespace keeps every forge's post-receive
169	// pipeline out of the loop, and the comparison apples to apples. Override
170	// with refs/heads/ to load that pipeline on purpose.
171	const DefaultRefNamespace = "refs/forgemark/"
172	
173	// Namespace returns the effective ref namespace: DefaultRefNamespace when
174	// unset, always with exactly one trailing slash so DestRef can concatenate.
175	func (w Workload) Namespace() string {
176		ns := w.RefNamespace
177		if ns == "" {
178			return DefaultRefNamespace
179		}
180		return strings.TrimRight(ns, "/") + "/"
181	}
182	
183	// CommitDesc describes the commit content shape, e.g. "1-10 x 2048B".
184	func (w Workload) CommitDesc() string {
185		return fmt.Sprintf("%d-%d x %dB", w.Commit.FilesMin, w.Commit.FilesMax, w.Commit.FileSize)
186	}
187	
188	// NewRunID returns a fresh run identifier. Nanosecond resolution so two runs
189	// started back-to-back (a server restarting a sweep) can't collide.
190	func NewRunID() string {
191		return "fm" + strconv.FormatInt(time.Now().UnixNano(), 36)
192	}
193	
194	// DestRef builds an agent's destination ref under namespace (already
195	// normalized by Workload.Namespace, trailing slash included), prepending
196	// branchPrefix verbatim before the run ID. Empty prefix reproduces the
197	// default name.
198	func DestRef(namespace, branchPrefix, runID string, c, i int) string {
199		return fmt.Sprintf("%s%s%s-c%d-a%d", namespace, branchPrefix, runID, c, i)
200	}
201	
202	// IsGitHubDotCom reports whether remote points at github.com (so the abuse
203	// warning + sha1 constraint apply). Any other host — GHES, GitLab, Gitea — is
204	// just a generic forge.
205	func IsGitHubDotCom(remote string) bool {
206		u, err := url.Parse(remote)
207		if err != nil {
208			return false
209		}
210		return strings.EqualFold(u.Hostname(), "github.com")
211	}

## 1. `drain-level-end` (in this checkout)

- **How it works:** each agent keeps its own running estimate of how long a push takes, and a separate one for clones. Before starting an operation it checks whether that operation is expected to finish before the window ends, and stops if not. The estimate jumps up straight away when a request is slower and comes down slowly when requests get faster. So when requests start queueing and slowing down, agents stop starting new work earlier, which is the case you described.
- **Hard stop:** in-flight operations now get up to 30s past the window end (`drainGrace`) before they're cancelled. Only requests that run well past their estimate get cancelled now, instead of everything in flight. `tokenCovers` counts that 30s per level, and I updated `TestTokenCovers` to match.
- **Effect on results:** throughput should come out about the same. Before, the push in flight at the window end was cancelled and not counted. Now it is simply never started.
- **Tests:** unit tests for the estimate, plus an end-to-end test against a slow HTTP server. It shows 1 cancelled request without the change and 0 with it.
- The demo runner isn't changed. Its requests are simulated, so the server sees no cancellations.

## 2. `push-options` (worktree at `../forgemark-push-options`)

- **Flag:** `-push-options` / `--push-options`, repeated once per option, like `git push -o`. I made it repeatable rather than comma-separated because real push options can contain commas (e.g. GitLab's `merge_request.*`).
- **Where it's sent:** every push forgemark makes. That's the measured pushes (branch/repo/session) and also the cleanup deletes (session ref deletes and the stale-ref sweep), so the server treats all of them the same way.
- **Validation:** an option containing a newline or NUL is rejected, as git itself does.
- **Tests:** an in-process go-git HTTP server records what each push sends, and the test checks the options arrive on both a push and a delete. It fails without the change.
- **Silent drop:** if the server doesn't advertise the `push-options` capability, go-git drops the options without an error, whereas `git` refuses the push. I noted this in the README rather than adding a check that fails hard.
- **Not included:** the option isn't available in the web server's run settings and isn't saved in result files. Both are easy to add if you want them.

Both fixes are ready, neither is committed yet, and format, vet, `go test -race ./...` and lint pass on both branches.

## `drain-level-end`: tail-bucket spike (in the scratch worktree)

The finding was right. Ops that finished during the drain were recorded after `measEnd`, and since periodic ticks stop at `measEnd`, the forced tail flush counted all of them against the small leftover `dt`, so the tail rate spiked.

- **Fix:** an op that finishes after the window end is no longer recorded. It still runs to completion, so the server never sees it cancelled. A new `windowClosed(ctx, end)` check replaces the old "cancelled" check in the branch, clone and session loops. The session push loop still deletes its session ref afterwards.
- **Why at the source and not in `runmgr`:** the live series and `summarize` now count the same set of ops, and nothing arrives after `measEnd`, so there is no spike to correct.
- **Trade-off:** those slow overrunning ops don't show up in latency percentiles. That's how stats worked before this branch, when they were cancelled. The predictive stop keeps them rare.
- **Test:** `TestAgentDropsOpsFinishingAfterWindowEnd` failed before the change and passes now. It checks there are no cancellations and no recorded sample for an op that overruns the window.

## `push-options`: capability check (in your checkout)

The finding was right. go-git only sends options the server advertises, and otherwise drops them while the push still succeeds.

- **Fix:** when `-push-options` is set, `NewRunner` fetches the receive-pack advertisement for every repo on every node before any write. If `push-options` isn't advertised, it refuses to start with a clear error. Every repo is checked because git's `receive.advertisePushOptions` setting is per repo. The advertisement is parsed with go-git's `packp.AdvRefs` decoder, not string matching. Without push options, nothing extra is probed.
- **Tests:** a parser test (capability present, missing, prefix-only near-miss, non-git reply), and a `NewRunner` test against a server without the capability and one with it. The `NewRunner` test fails without the wiring.
- **Docs:** I updated the README row and the flag help to say the run refuses to start.

## Proposed commits

**`drain-level-end`** (`internal/bench/{agent.go,agent_test.go,session.go}`):
```
bench: don't record ops that finish after the window end

Ops that overran the window finished during the drain and were recorded
after measEnd. Periodic ticks stop there, so the forced tail flush put
every drain completion into a bucket whose dt stops at the window end,
spiking the live and persisted rate. Such ops still run to completion,
so the server sees no cancellation, but go unrecorded, matching what
summarize counted before the drain existed.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
```

**`push-options`** (`README.md`, `cmd/forgemark/main.go`, `internal/bench/{agent_test.go,endpoint.go,runner.go}`):
```
bench: refuse -push-options when the server doesn't advertise them

go-git drops push options a server doesn't advertise and the push still
succeeds, so a requested ci.skip could silently vanish and the run would
measure different remote work. NewRunner now probes the receive-pack
advertisement of every repo on every node and fails before any write
when push-options is missing.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
```
